summary.text: The median of a set of numbers is the value separating the higher half from the lower half, so it can be thought of as the middle value.
For a finite list of numbers, it is the middle number when they are arranged in order from smallest to greatest.
The median is not skewed by a small proportion of extreme values, so median income may describe the center of incomes better than the mean.

facts.label: Finding it
facts.value: The middle number after sorting smallest to greatest

facts.label: Rich earners
facts.value: Raising the largest incomes alone has no effect

facts.label: Ranked grades
facts.value: Can be found for letter grades from F to A

facts.value: Computable without knowing the extreme results

items.prompt: Five test scores are 1, 3, 5, 7 and 30. What is their median?
items.explain: The median is the middle number when arranged in order from smallest to greatest, which is 5 here.

items.prompt: The richest person in a town doubles their income and no one else's income changes. What happens to the town's median income?

options.label: It does not change
It doubles
It rises slightly
It falls

items.explain: Increases in the largest incomes alone have no effect on the median.

items.prompt: A teacher has only letter grades from F to A, no points. Can she find a median grade?

options.label: No, a median needs numbers to add
Yes, ranking the grades is enough
Yes, but only after turning them into points
No, only the most common grade works

items.explain: The median is well-defined for any ordered data, so it can be applied to ranked grades that are not numerical.

items.prompt: Four students are ranked by grade and the two middle ones got a B and a C. Where does the median fall?

options.label: Exactly at B, since it comes first
Exactly at C, since it comes last
At A, the top grade
Halfway between B and C

items.explain: With an even number of students, the result might be halfway between grades.

items.prompt: In a problem-solving test, a few people never finished in time, so their times are unknown. Can a median time still be found?

options.label: Yes, since it rests on the middle data and not the extreme results
No, every result must be known
No, unless the unfinished people are removed first
Yes, but only by guessing their times

items.explain: Because the median is based on the middle data, the extreme results need not be known to calculate it.

items.prompt: A teacher splits her class into two equal-sized groups, lower and higher scorers. What is the score at the dividing line?

options.label: The mean
The mode
The range
The median

items.explain: The median is the value that partitions a set into two equal parts, separating the higher half from the lower half.

paragraphs.heading: The middle value
paragraphs.text: The median is the value that splits a set of numbers into a higher half and a lower half. For a set of data you can think of it as the middle value. To find it for a finite list, sort the numbers from smallest to largest and take the one in the middle.

paragraphs.heading: Not pulled by extremes
paragraphs.text: Its key strength, compared with the mean, is that a small share of extreme values does not drag it around, so it often gives a better picture of the center. Income shows why. If only the very largest incomes rise, the median does not move at all. For this reason the median plays a central part in robust statistics.

paragraphs.heading: When extremes are unknown
paragraphs.text: The median is the measure to reach for when extreme values deserve less weight: when a distribution is skewed, when the extremes are not known, or when outliers may be mistakes in measuring or copying. Because it depends only on the middle of the data, you never need the exact extreme results. Picture a psychology test that times how long people take to solve a problem. If a few people never solve it in the time allowed, the median time can still be worked out.

paragraphs.heading: Beyond numbers
paragraphs.text: The median only needs data that can be put in order, with no measure of distance between values. So it works for letter grades from F to A, which can be ranked but are not numbers. With an odd number of students, the median is one particular grade. With an even number, it may land halfway between two grades.

paragraphs.heading: A family of cut points
paragraphs.text: The median belongs to a family of cut points. Because it divides a set into two equal parts, it is called the 2-quantile. In the same way it is the 2nd quartile, the 5th decile and the 50th percentile.

paragraphs.heading: Medians of distributions
paragraphs.text: For a symmetric distribution with a single peak, the median equals the mode. In a normal distribution the mean, median and mode are all the same. For a uniform distribution on the interval from a to b, the median is (a + b) / 2, which is also its mean. For an exponential distribution with rate λ, the median is λ⁻¹ln 2.

paragraphs.heading: The price of robustness
paragraphs.text: The median is a popular summary in descriptive statistics because it is simple to grasp, easy to compute and a robust stand-in for the mean. There is a cost. For large samples from a normal distribution, the median has a 64% efficiency compared with the mean, meaning its variance is about 50% larger. The sample mean is the more efficient choice only when the data are free of contamination from heavy-tailed distributions or mixtures of distributions.
